newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian auto firms 1st half net seen leaping 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indian auto firms 1st half net seen leaping 40 pct.

text.p: India's top three listed auto companies' profits are seen riding high on all around growth in sales in the first half to September 30, 1996, and the sector will continue to outperform others, analysts said on Wednesday.
"Volume growth in these three auto companies is much higher than for companies in any other sector," said Prashant Reddy, auto analyst at ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec).

Reddy and other analysts gave their views following a Reuters poll of 14 leading securities houses released on Tuesday that showed net profit for the auto sector forecast to leap 40 percent in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March).

The poll projected a combined average net profit of 6,721 million rupees ($188.3 million) in the first half of 1996/97 -- from 4,779.2 million a year ago -- for scooter maker Bajaj Auto, truckmaker TELCO and utility vehicles maker Mahindra & Mahindra.
Reddy said volume growth would be around 23-24 percent for the three firms.
"This should translate into sales growth in excess of 30 percent in the first half," he said.

India's largest car maker, Maruti Udyog Ltd, is not listed on the bourses. The company, which is equally owned by the Indian government and Japan's Suzuki Motor Company, accounts for over 70 percent of the car market.
The poll forecast a combined average jump of 28 percent in first half net sales for the auto firms.
But first-half profits of leading Indian companies that make up the benchmark Bombay stocks index are likely to see a sharp slowdown in growth to an average 20.6 percent, the poll found.
"The auto sector emerges a clear out-performer, as falling commodity prices have caused a negative trend in several other index stocks, said Subra Subramanian, director at securities firm H.G. Asia.
"Quite a bit of unfilled vehicle demand from last year and continued growth in sales of medium and heavy commercial vehicles will boost TELCO's bottomline," he said.
Analysts said auto firms emerged unscathed from a 12.9 percent minimum alternate tax (MAT) on book profits that was introduced in India's 1996/97 budget.
"They are all high tax payers and were not affected by MAT," said Sandeep Talwar, analyst at SSKI Securities.
Talwar said a reduction in corporate surcharge -- also announced in the budget in July -- would boost 1996/97 profits of these auto companies by 1.5 to 3.0 percent.
I-Sec's Reddy said he expected the auto sector to remain an out-performer in the coming year.
"We are still bullish and expect the outperformance to continue, but we are sticking to the leaders in the segment," he said.
(in millions of rupees)
NET PROFIT SALES
BAJAJ AUTO ----PAT seen up 35.8%, sales up 24.3%
M&M ----PAT seen up 41.7%, sales up 22.1%
TELCO ----PAT seen up 44%, sales up 31.4%
($One = 35.70 rupees)
